log.text: Light Screen up on P1's side
Floette used Light of Ruin → Klefki
Light Screen ended on P1's side
Floette used Light of Ruin → Incineroar

decisions.rationale: Lead Metagross + Rotom-Wash: Metagross Mega Evolves and outspeeds Floette-Mega (178 vs 154 max), threatening OHKO with Tough Claws Meteor Mash. Rotom-Wash is immune to Garchomp's EQ, can burn it or Hydro Pump. Klefki in back provides Prankster screens and Thunder Wave to cripple Floette-Mega if it survives. Incineroar offers Fake Out disruption, Intimidate for Garchomp, and Flare Blitz as secondary Fairy coverage. Dragapult and Corviknight are less essential here—Metagross already covers Floette and Rotom handles Garchomp/Talonflame.
decisions.notebook: Floette-Mega is the opponent's sole win condition; eliminate it at any cost. Opponent leads aggressively with Floette + Garchomp, often double-Protecting Garchomp to stall. Garchomp spams Stomping Tantrum after failed moves; burn cripples it. Milotic runs Icy Wind for speed control, Hydro Pump, and Sitrus Berry; it can surprise with special bulk. Talonflame has Focus Sash and Tailwind but dies to strong Electric moves before Sash activates. Opponent did not bring Scrafty or Goodra this game but may bring Scrafty for Fake Out and Intimidate next game—prepare Fairy countermeasures. Rotom-Wash cleans late-game with Leftovers, especially if Garchomp is burned. Screens from Klefki are valuable but draw early pressure; apply Thunder Wave before it faints if possible.

decisions.rationale: Lead Tailwind plus Floette-Eternal’s special pressure into the previously shown Klefki/Rotom-Wash opening, while preserving Garchomp for Mega Metagross and Goodra-Hisui as the durable special attacker for Rotom-Wash and Dragapult.
decisions.notebook: Opponent previously brought Klefki, Rotom-Wash, Mega Metagross, and Life Orb Dragapult; Incineroar and Corviknight were not brought. Expect early Prankster Reflect/Light Screen and Rotom-Wash Will-O-Wisp/Protect/Leftovers. Preserve a special attacker for Rotom-Wash; Garchomp is valuable into Mega Metagross.

decisions.rationale: Talonflame's Gale Wings Tailwind is unstoppable turn 1, so I play around it. Metagross Mega Evolves and Bullet Punches Floette: +1 priority ensures it connects before Floette moves, forcing either a Protect or dealing ~40-78% chip (Tough Claws boosted) into their win condition. Rotom-Wash Volt Switches Talonflame to break Focus Sash and pivot — even if Floette Protects, I still strip Sash and reposition. Under Tailwind, Mega Metagross (Speed 178→356) outspeeds Mega Floette (max 338), setting up a potential Meteor Mash KO next turn. Pivoting Rotom to Incineroar brings Intimidate and Fake Out pressure for turn 2.
decisions.notebook: Floette-Mega is the opponent's sole win condition; eliminate it at any cost. Opponent leads aggressively with Floette + Garchomp, often double-Protecting Garchomp to stall. Garchomp spams Stomping Tantrum after failed moves; burn cripples it. Milotic runs Icy Wind for speed control, Hydro Pump, and Sitrus Berry; it can surprise with special bulk. Talonflame has Focus Sash and Tailwind but dies to strong Electric moves before Sash activates. Opponent did not bring Scrafty or Goodra this game but may bring Scrafty for Fake Out and Intimidate next game—prepare Fairy countermeasures. Rotom-Wash cleans late-game with Leftovers, especially if Garchomp is burned. Screens from Klefki are valuable but draw early pressure; apply Thunder Wave before it faints if possible. Mega Metagross Speed 178 outspeeds Mega Floette (max 169) under Tailwind.

decisions.rationale: Metagross survives any realistic double-target this turn (Heat Wave max 53.5% + Fairy Aura Light of Ruin max 58.4% = 111.9% only on dual max rolls with Mega Evolution). Keeping Metagross in preserves the Meteor Mash OHKO threat on Floette. Switching Rotom to Klefki walls Floette's entire moveset (15–35% per hit), enables Prankster Thunder Wave to permanently neutralize Tailwind, and sets Light Screen to protect Metagross from Heat Wave. Incineroar offers no speed control and takes 39–55% from Moonblast with no threatening response. We do not forfeit up 1–0.
decisions.notebook: Floette-Eternal can Mega Evolve into Floette-Mega (Fairy Aura, 155 SpA), boosting all Fairy moves on the field — including Klefki's Dazzling Gleam. Metagross-Mega Meteor Mash is a guaranteed OHKO on Floette-Mega. Thunder Wave on Floette-Mega is the highest-priority status play. Garchomp and Milotic remain unrevealed in game 2; burn Garchomp on sight to neutralize Stomping Tantrum. Opponent may bring Scrafty (Fake Out + Intimidate) in game 3 — lead Fairy-strong.

decisions.rationale: Protect Floette from Mega Metagross’s immediate Steel pressure while priority Tailwind establishes a strong speed advantage without risking either lead unnecessarily.
decisions.notebook: Opponent previously brought Klefki, Rotom-Wash, Mega Metagross, and Life Orb Dragapult; Incineroar and Corviknight were not brought. Expect Prankster screens and Rotom-Wash Will-O-Wisp/Protect/Leftovers. Preserve a special attacker for Rotom-Wash; Garchomp is valuable into Mega Metagross.

selection: Light Screen (your side, including ally Metagross-Mega)
decisions.rationale: Bullet Punch breaks Talonflame's Focus Sash at +1 priority before it can move. Klefki's Prankster Light Screen goes up immediately after, reducing the incoming Heat Wave (super-effective on both allies) by ⅓ for 8 turns with Light Clay. This preserves both Pokémon's HP, leaves Talonflame at 1 HP to be picked off next turn, and neuters Floette-Mega's special attacks for the remainder of the field. Safe, high-percentage play while up 1-0 in the series.

selection: Light of Ruin -> foe 2 (Klefki) + Mega Evolve
decisions.rationale: Mega Evolve and apply maximum immediate special pressure to Klefki while Heat Wave damages both Steel-types and can punish any non-Light Screen Klefki line.
decisions.notebook: Opponent has again shown Klefki, Rotom-Wash, Mega Metagross, and Life Orb Dragapult as its four in this game; prioritize physical pressure into screens and retain special coverage for Rotom-Wash.

decisions.rationale: Bring Garchomp: Tailwind gives immediate physical Ground pressure into both revealed Steel-types despite Light Screen, while preserving Floette's special coverage for Rotom-Wash.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 opponent’s four are confirmed as Mega Metagross, Klefki, Rotom-Wash, and Life Orb Dragapult. Prioritize physical pressure through screens and preserve Floette’s special coverage for Rotom-Wash.

decisions.rationale: Klefki is guaranteed KO'd by Garchomp Earthquake under Tailwind regardless of our play. We extract maximum value by using Prankster Thunder Wave on Floette-Mega before Klefki faints, permanently crippling its Speed and adding a 25% full-para chance. Metagross-Mega Protects to avoid the 61-91% from Earthquake plus potential Floette chip, staying at full HP. Next turn Tailwind has 1 turn left; we bring Rotom-Wash (Levitate immune to EQ) alongside a healthy Metagross to clean up the paralysed Floette and Garchomp.

Incineroar's Intimidate immediately cuts Garchomp's Attack, ensuring Metagross-Mega survives any combination of Stomping Tantrum + Moonblast this turn (worst case ~65-92% with -1 Atk and Light Screen). Without Intimidate, Metagross-Mega risks being KO'd before moving (86-122%). Rotom-Wash's Ground immunity is appealing but leaves Metagross-Mega exposed to full-power Stomping Tantrum. Incineroar also brings Fake Out and Parting Shot for future turns, and Sitrus Berry helps it survive a -1 Stomping Tantrum. Metagross-Mega can then OHKO Floette-Mega with Meteor Mash next turn once it survives the double-target.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Klefki fainted turn 3 after setting Light Screen (7 turns remain). Opponent Tailwind has 2 turns left. Metagross-Mega OHKOs Floette-Mega with Meteor Mash. Incineroar Intimidate not yet used this game. Garchomp is Life Orb Jolly; burn it on sight to neutralize Stomping Tantrum. Opponent's last unrevealed is one of Milotic/Scrafty/Goodra-Hisui. If Scrafty appears in game 3, lead Fairy-strong.

decisions.rationale: Protect Floette from Bullet Punch while Garchomp’s Stomping Tantrum guarantees the KO on the weakened Klefki, removing priority Thunder Wave and Light Screen support before Rotom-Wash enters.

Fake Out Floette-Mega to prevent its attack; Meteor Mash guarantees the KO on Floette-Mega from 76% (102.8-193.3%). Garchomp's Earthquake deals 41-61% to Metagross and 50-71% to Incineroar through Light Screen and -1 Atk, which both survive comfortably. This removes the Fairy Aura boost and Mega threat immediately, leaving a 2v1 with Tailwind expiring after this turn. Floette's Protect is on reduced success rate after two consecutive uses, making an attack far more likely.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Klefki fainted turn 3 after setting Light Screen (7 turns remain). Opponent Tailwind has 1 turn left. Metagross-Mega OHKOs Floette-Mega with Meteor Mash. Incineroar Intimidate used on entry. Garchomp is Life Orb Jolly; burn it on sight. Opponent's last unrevealed is one of Milotic/Scrafty/Goodra-Hisui. If Scrafty appears in game 3, lead Fairy-strong.

decisions.rationale: Preserve Floette for its crucial Rotom matchup and use Garchomp's reliable Protect to deny the most likely Fake Out/Metagross pressure turn. Goodra enters safely against Metagross's resisted Steel attacks.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 has revealed Mega Metagross, Klefki, Incineroar, and Rotom-Wash; preserve Mega Floette for special pressure into Rotom-Wash and avoid sacrificing it into Mega Metagross Steel priority.

decisions.rationale: Metagross Protect scouts safely while Incineroar Parting Shots Garchomp to -2 Atk/-1 SpA, then pivots into Rotom-Wash. Rotom-Wash is immune to EQ (Levitate) and resists Fire, walling both foes. Light Screen remains up. This preserves Metagross's HP, cripples Garchomp further, and sets up a dominant Metagross+Rotom board against a debuffed Garchomp and a 49% Goodra. Even if both foes target Incineroar, Sitrus Berry ensures survival through EQ+Draco Meteor.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Klefki fainted turn 3 after setting Light Screen. Metagross-Mega OHKOs Floette-Mega with Meteor Mash. Incineroar Intimidate used on entry. Garchomp is Life Orb Jolly; burn it on sight. Goodra-Hisui is Modest Leftovers Sap Sipper. Opponent's last unrevealed is one of Milotic/Scrafty/Goodra-Hisui — Goodra revealed. If Scrafty appears in game 3, lead Fairy-strong.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Focus the two strongest available attacks into Mega Metagross, the key obstacle to preserving Floette’s endgame; Stomping Tantrum avoids damaging Goodra while applying the most immediate single-target Ground pressure.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 opponent brought Mega Metagross, Incineroar, Rotom-Wash, and Klefki; Klefki is eliminated. Mega Metagross carries Meteor Mash, Zen Headbutt, Bullet Punch, and Protect; Incineroar carries Fake Out, Flare Blitz, Parting Shot, and Darkest Lariat; Rotom-Wash carries Hydro Pump, Volt Switch, Will-O-Wisp, and Protect. Preserve Mega Floette for special pressure into Rotom-Wash and avoid exposing it to Mega Metagross Steel priority.

decisions.rationale: Metagross survives EQ+Flamethrower without crit (63.7–94.3% combined under Light Screen). Meteor Mash chips Goodra to 13.7–32.5% while Will-O-Wisp (85%) burns Garchomp, stacking with its existing -2 Atk to render it nearly harmless. Opponent has no bench to pivot, so burn sticks. Next turn Bullet Punch can pick off a weakened Goodra.
Protect Garchomp from the likely combined Meteor Mash and Hydro Pump pressure while Goodra safely chips Mega Metagross, the key Steel-type preventing a Floette endgame.

Metagross Meteor Mash into Goodra-Hisui guarantees a KO if Goodra doesn't Protect (33.7-61.9% vs 27% HP). Metagross outspeeds both foes, so Goodra can't Flamethrower before being KO'd. Rotom Will-O-Wisp into Garchomp permanently cripples it; even at -2 Atk, burn stacks multiplicatively, rendering Garchomp near-harmless. If Goodra Protects, Meteor Mash is blocked but Garchomp gets burned. If Garchomp Protects instead, Goodra still dies. Rotom is immune to Earthquake so Garchomp can't hit both slots with spread. Combined damage from Flamethrower + Stomping Tantrum could threaten Metagross, but Metagross moves first and removes Goodra before it can attack.

Protect preserves Goodra from Mega Metagross’s guaranteed Meteor Mash KO while Garchomp applies its strongest ally-safe damage to Metagross; Earthquake has no damage advantage here because of spread reduction and would also hit Goodra.

Metagross Meteor Mash into Goodra is a guaranteed KO (33.7% min into 33% HP) and Metagross moves first. Goodra's Protect is at reduced success (≈1/3) after using it last turn. Even if Goodra Protects, it risks failing. Garchomp will likely KO Metagross with Stomping Tantrum afterwards, but trading our 12% Metagross for their 33% Goodra is highly favorable—Metagross was going to be KOed anyway by either foe. Rotom Hydro Pump into Garchomp deals 27–48% chip, safe from Ground immunity. After the trade the board is Rotom (full) + Incineroar (full, with Fake Out available) vs Garchomp (~26–47%, burned, -2 Atk) + Floette-Mega (76%), a winning endgame. If opponent switches Goodra to Floette, Meteor Mash OHKOs Floette instead, which is even better.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Stomping Tantrum guarantees Mega Metagross’s KO if it does not Protect, while Goodra’s Protect most safely denies its likely Meteor Mash and Rotom pressure; retaining Goodra is valuable against the remaining special attackers.

Fake Out on Goodra-Hisui guarantees it cannot act this turn, while Hydro Pump on Garchomp is a guaranteed KO from 17% if Garchomp doesn't Protect. If Garchomp does Protect (full accuracy, last used turn 6), we still flinch Goodra and face a 2v1 next turn with Garchomp at 17% burned and Goodra at 39% — an overwhelmingly winning position. Even if Goodra were to attack, Draco Meteor through Light Screen does at most ~52% to Rotom and ~47% to Incineroar, never OHKOing either.
Preserve the low-HP burned Garchomp through the expected Fake Out or Water pressure while bringing Mega Floette in safely to threaten Rotom-Wash once Light Screen expires.
decisions.notebook: Opponent's Game 2 brought Mega Metagross, Klefki, Incineroar, and Rotom-Wash; Dragapult and Corviknight were not brought. Incineroar has Fake Out, Flare Blitz, Parting Shot, and Darkest Lariat with Intimidate and Sitrus Berry. Rotom-Wash has Hydro Pump, Volt Switch, Will-O-Wisp, and Protect with Levitate and Leftovers. Klefki used Prankster Light Screen, Reflect, Thunder Wave, and Dazzling Gleam with Light Clay. Mega Metagross has Meteor Mash, Zen Headbutt, Bullet Punch, and Protect. Preserve Mega Floette to pressure Rotom-Wash with Energy Ball and avoid exposing it to Steel priority when Metagross is present.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp dies to burn at end of turn but still moves before Rotom-Wash. Hydro Pump guarantees the KO on Garchomp (27-48% into 11%) so it can't get a final attack off next turn. Parting Shot into Floette-Mega drops its SpA to -1, neutering its offensive pressure for the rest of the game. Even if both foes double-target Incineroar this turn (Moonblast 61-86% + Stomping Tantrum 15-22%), Sitrus Berry keeps Incineroar alive. Result: 2v1 with a debuffed Floette-Mega and both my Pokémon healthy enough to clean up.
Energy Ball gives the strongest immediate chance to remove Rotom-Wash, the key threat to the endgame; Stomping Tantrum adds the most meaningful available damage into Incineroar.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Game 2 brought Mega Metagross, Klefki, Incineroar, and Rotom-Wash; Dragapult and Corviknight were not brought. Incineroar has Fake Out, Flare Blitz, Parting Shot, and Darkest Lariat with Intimidate and Sitrus Berry. Rotom-Wash has Hydro Pump, Volt Switch, Will-O-Wisp, and Protect with Levitate and Leftovers. Klefki used Prankster Light Screen, Reflect, Thunder Wave, and Dazzling Gleam with Light Clay. Mega Metagross has Meteor Mash, Zen Headbutt, Bullet Punch, and Protect. Preserve Mega Floette to pressure Rotom-Wash with Energy Ball and avoid exposing it to Steel priority when Metagross is present.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Rotom Protect survives the guaranteed KO from Floette Energy Ball or Goodra Draco Meteor. Incineroar Flare Blitz is a guaranteed OHKO on 39% Goodra-Hisui. If opponent targets Rotom with Energy Ball (blocked) and Incineroar with Draco Meteor, Incineroar drops to ~9–32% HP, Sitrus Berry triggers, and next turn it's 2v1 against a –1 SpA Floette-Mega — Flare Blitz plus Hydro Pump secure the series. The only losing line is if opponent predicts Protect and doubles Incineroar with Moonblast + Draco Meteor, which can KO through Sitrus; that read is unlikely when Rotom is at 25% and an obvious Energy Ball target.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Klefki fainted turn 3 after setting Light Screen. Metagross-Mega OHKOs Floette-Mega with Meteor Mash. Incineroar Intimidate used on entry. Garchomp is Life Orb Jolly; burn it on sight. Goodra-Hisui is Modest Leftovers Sap Sipper. Opponent's last unrevealed is either Milotic or Scrafty — both not brought game 2. If Scrafty appears in game 3, lead Fairy-strong.

decisions.rationale: Light of Ruin is the only immediate line with a chance to remove Incineroar before it can eliminate Goodra; Protect preserves Goodra if Incineroar survives the hit.
decisions.notebook: Incineroar is Adamant Intimidate with Fake Out, Flare Blitz, Parting Shot, and Darkest Lariat plus Sitrus Berry. Rotom-Wash is Bold Levitate with Hydro Pump, Volt Switch, Will-O-Wisp, Protect, and Leftovers. Mega Floette’s Fairy Aura-boosted Energy Ball reliably threatens Rotom-Wash, while Incineroar’s Flare Blitz is a major threat to Goodra-Hisui.

decisions.rationale: Rotom-Wash is alone at 31% HP against Floette-Mega (18%) and Goodra-Hisui (44%). Floette-Mega is guaranteed faster (122–154 vs 108) and OHKOs with Energy Ball or Moonblast before Rotom can move. Hydro Pump would KO Floette but Rotom never gets to use it. Protect has a 1/3 consecutive success rate and even if it works, the following turn Floette still outspeeds and OHKOs. No available switch-in for Incineroar's slot. The position is unwinnable; forfeiting preserves mental energy for game 3 with the series lead intact.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 lost. Series score 1-1 going into game 3. Opponent's full team: Garchomp (Life Orb Jolly), Talonflame (Focus Sash Jolly), Floette-Mega (Modest), Goodra-Hisui (Leftovers Modest Sap Sipper), Milotic (Sitrus Berry Bold Competitive), Scrafty (Lum Berry Careful Intimidate). In game 3, lead with Fairy-strong options if Scrafty appears. Floette-Mega is a major threat with Fairy Aura-boosted Light of Ruin and Energy Ball coverage. Goodra-Hisui is specially bulky with Sap Sipper blocking Spore/sleep powder. Burn Garchomp on sight.

decisions.rationale: Energy Ball is a guaranteed KO on Rotom-Wash if Floette moves, while Draco Meteor provides a second guaranteed-damage KO line if Rotom-Wash acts first and removes Floette. This covers the uncertain Speed order with the highest accuracy available on Floette.
decisions.notebook: Rotom-Wash is Bold Levitate with Hydro Pump, Volt Switch, Will-O-Wisp, Protect, and Leftovers. Mega Floette's Fairy Aura-boosted Energy Ball is a reliable Rotom-Wash answer; account for Rotom potentially outrunning Mega Floette. Hisuian Goodra carries Acid Spray, Draco Meteor, Flamethrower, and Protect with Leftovers.

reflections.summary: Metagross-Mega fell early to repeated SpDef drops from Acid Spray (not shown in turns but implied) or direct Flamethrower damage, leaving no reliable answer to Floette-Mega's Light of Ruin. Screens from Klefki provided temporary mitigation, but Garchomp's Stomping Tantrum broke Klefki quickly and Goodra's double Protect stalled out Metagross. The loss of Metagross allowed Floette to sweep with support from Goodra's constant pressure and healing.
reflections.adjustment: Next game, prioritize keeping Metagross healthy to check Floette-Mega. Lead with Fake Out + Bullet Punch to deny Talonflame's Tailwind, but set Reflect with Klefki early to neuter Garchomp. Use Parting Shot more aggressively to pivot Metagross out of Flamethrower or Earthquakes, saving it for the endgame. Target Garchomp swiftly with Will-O-Wisp after scouting Protects, and avoid letting Goodra chain Protects by doubling into it when it attempts to stall.
reflections.notebook: Game 2 lost; series 1-1. Opponent tendencies: Talonflame leads and immediately sets Tailwind. Floette-Mega uses Protect on its first turn out to Mega Evolve safely. Goodra switches into special attackers and may double Protect under pressure. Garchomp spams Stomping Tantrum and uses Protect to block status. In Game 3, expect similar or a switch to Scrafty/Milotic. Lead with Fairy-strong pressure if Scrafty appears. Plan to preserve Metagross for Floette; use Reflect to weaken Garchomp; burn Garchomp on sight but scout Protects. Rotom-Wash is key for pivoting and burning, but must avoid Energy Ball from Floette.

reflections.summary: Won by using the Floette-Mega/Garchomp/Goodra-Hisui endgame to remove Klefki and Mega Metagross, then exploiting Floette's Fairy Aura-boosted coverage to clean through Incineroar and leave Rotom-Wash in range. The brought four and Mega Floette were well suited: Talonflame secured early Tailwind, Garchomp pressured Metagross, and Goodra absorbed its attacks while providing Flamethrower pressure.
reflections.adjustment: Preserve Talonflame's Focus Sash/Tailwind value more carefully against Rotom-Wash Volt Switch plus Mega Metagross Bullet Punch; consider Protecting Talonflame on turn 1 or leading a bulkier pair if denying immediate Tailwind loss is important.
reflections.notebook: Opponent brought Mega Metagross, Klefki, Incineroar, and Rotom-Wash in game 2; Dragapult and Corviknight were not brought. Klefki uses Prankster Light Screen, Thunder Wave, and likely Reflect/Dazzling Gleam; prioritize denying or removing it before screens compound. Incineroar has Fake Out, Intimidate, Parting Shot, Flare Blitz, and Darkest Lariat with Sitrus Berry, and used Fake Out/Parting Shot repeatedly for pivot disruption. Mega Metagross has Meteor Mash, Zen Headbutt, Bullet Punch, and Protect; Hisuian Goodra resists Meteor Mash and Flamethrower plus Garchomp Ground pressure can wear it down. Rotom-Wash can pair Volt Switch with Metagross Bullet Punch to immediately pressure Talonflame.
